verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The display's closest counterpart is LinearWaveResidual.cartesianLinearResidual (line 511), which is the paper's operator term for term, sign for sign, in the paper's own Cartesian notation and real-valued: temporalDerivative a t x is d_t w, spatialDerivative a t x (B (t,x)) is (u_B.grad)w, spatialDerivative B t x (a (t,x)) is (w.grad)u_B, pressureGradient p t x is grad pi, and -eps * spatialLaplacian a t x is -Delta w, with spatialDerivative, pressureGradient and spatialLaplacian the Euclidean operators of ProblemStatement (lines 59, 71, 76). The single encoding choice is that the viscosity is a free real parameter eps where the paper's display fixes the coefficient of Delta w at 1; the paper's L is the eps = 1 instance, and eps is instantiated as c.operators.epsilon n at the call sites in CorrectionStep. The repository also carries the same operator in two conjugated forms: cylindricalLinearResidual (503), the frame-component version, which cartesianLinearResidual_cylindrical (534) proves equal to the Cartesian one under the cylindrical chart, and the complexified-component linearResidual (57) used in the harmonic calculus, whose five terms match the same dictionary (along Vt is d_t, transport B a is (u_B.grad)w, transport a B is (w.grad)u_B, gradient p is grad pi, -(eps) * cylindricalVectorLaplacian a is -Delta w) and whose real form is recovered by realComponentLinearResidual_eq_cylindrical. The same five terms appear once more inlined, unnamed, on the right-hand side of ResidualCalculus.navierStokesResidual_add_sub.
